{"path":"SOLUTION.md","content":"# Solution

Two bugs in `lrucache/cache.py`:

1. **`get` did not refresh recency.** A successful `get` returned the value
   without moving the key to the MRU end of the `OrderedDict`, so recently
   read entries were still evicted as if untouched. Fixed by calling
   `self._data.move_to_end(key)` before returning the value.

2. **`put` evicted even when updating an existing key.** The capacity check
   ran unconditionally, so updating a key in a full cache evicted the LRU
   entry even though no new slot was needed. Fixed by only evicting when the
   key is not already present (`if key not in self._data and ...`).

content:
All 6 tests pass. Two fixes in `lrucache/cache.py`:

- `get()` now calls `move_to_end(key)` on a hit, so reads count as "use" and refresh recency.
- `put()` only evicts the LRU entry when inserting a *new* key into a full cache — updating an existing key no longer evicts an innocent entry.

Root causes documented in `SOLUTION.md`.
